solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Device offering speed of sound on military aircraft between Kent and Tyneside?

indicators.note: between says the aircraft pieces sit inside the two regions

parts.note: Kent is in the south-east of England, abbreviated SE
Tyneside is in the north-east of England, abbreviated NE

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it

parts.note: a wing is an air force unit of aircraft
Mach 1 is the speed of sound, written with the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A supersonic jet flying the length of England from Kent to Tyneside.
explanation.walkthrough: SE and NE are compass abbreviations for the regions. 'between' puts WING plus MACH I inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewing machine is a mechanical appliance, so it is a fair example of a device.

clue.text: Lug noble European around house

indicators.note: around says the noble and European pieces go about the house

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A titled European lugging stuff round his house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lug' looks like a verb, to carry, but it is British slang for an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Lug is informal British for the ear, and an earhole is the ear or its opening.

clue.text: College group about three miles south of climber

indicators.note: in a down clue south of means placed below

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
a league is an old distance of roughly three miles

explanation.surface: A school party a few miles south of a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' suggests a mountaineer, but it is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League is an association of eight elite American universities.

clue.text: Turning maybe, about to flatten lizard

indicators.note: Turning means the abbreviation for example is reversed

parts.note: eg, for example, means maybe
C, circa, means about
to KO, knock out, is to flatten an opponent

explanation.surface: Someone turning, perhaps, about to squash a reptile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reverses EG to GE. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Geckos are small climbing reptiles of the lizard family.

clue.text: This stops fire using spray I found in unwrapped package

indicators.note: found in says the spray and I sit inside the remainder
unwrapped strips the outer letters off the package word

parts.note: a parcel is a package
mist is a fine spray
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fire extinguisher's spray found inside an opened parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' suggests flames, but the armistice stops gunfire; 'This' points the whole definition at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a truce, an agreement by warring sides to cease shooting.

clue.text: Serious actor playing villainous roles

definitions.meaning: weighty, grave, as in a ... discussion
in theatre and film the villain or the actor who plays such parts

explanation.surface: A grave performer typecast as the bad guy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means grave or weighty, and in show business it is the villain's part or its player.

clue.text: Almost gets up on docked horse, so falls

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above
in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so backwards
Almost drops the final letter

parts.note: to gain is to get

indicators.note: docked, like a horse's tail, means its last letter is cut

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: Someone nearly climbs onto a tailless horse and therefore tumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts GAINS to GAIN and 'up' reverses it to NIAG; 'docked' cuts ARAB to ARA.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: Hurt leg to begin with? Wrong on both counts

parts.note: in cricket the leg side is the opposite of the off side, so a wrong leg is off
the opposite of to begin is to end, so the wrong version gives end

explanation.surface: Someone who hurt a leg early on and got it wrong twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong on both counts' tells you to swap each piece for its opposite: leg side becomes off side, begin becomes end.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend someone is to upset or hurt their feelings.

clue.text: Air about one's spiritual knowledge

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so read backwards

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
one is I, and one's is short for one is, giving I and S

explanation.surface: An aura about someone's inner wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses SONG to GNOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnosis is esoteric knowledge of spiritual truths, central to Gnostic belief.

clue.text: Before end of rally, keep score — and again?

indicators.note: Before places the castle word ahead of the rally's final letter

parts.note: a keep is the stronghold of a castle, a fort

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of rally

explanation.surface: Holding on to a score just before the end of a tennis rally.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so a score and again is twice twenty. The tennis surface hints at the score of forty too.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty doubled gives the number, a score being an old word for twenty.

clue.text: Egomaniac sent out what?

indicators.note: sent out suggests the letters of Egomaniac are dispersed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone baffled that a self-obsessed person was sent away.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal requests to repeat something not heard or not believed.

clue.text: Sensitive old US vice-president backed English common sense

indicators.note: backed tells us to read the vice-president's name backwards

parts.note: Al Gore was US vice-president under Clinton
nous is common sense

explanation.surface: A touchy former American vice-president supported by English good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Al Gore was Bill Clinton's vice-president; 'backed' sends his name the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes bodily zones especially sensitive to arousal.

clue.text: Certainly welcoming retired artist for a long time

indicators.note: welcoming says the affirmative takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: yes is an affirmative, certainly

indicators.note: retired means the artist abbreviation goes backwards

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Assuredly welcoming a painter who has retired after a long career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' looks like the painter's career ending, but it reverses the artist. 'for' is a link, since 'for a long time' would not swap for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, years means an extended period, as in 'it took years'.

clue.text: Searches for doctor by borders

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: edges are borders

explanation.surface: Hunting for a physician along the margins.
explanation.definitionFit: To dredge a river or harbour is to search its bed by scraping it.

clue.text: Food presented by expert in painful promotion

indicators.note: in puts the expert inside the painful word

parts.note: sore means painful
a dab, or dab hand, is an expert
an ad promotes a product

explanation.surface: Something presented by a specialist in an excruciating advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presented by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda bread is an Irish loaf raised with bicarbonate of soda, so it is a food.

clue.text: Lunatic half-responds with air raids

indicators.note: lunatic means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
half takes one half of responds, here its second four letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A madman half-answers with talk of bombing attacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The back half of responds is ONDS; with AIR it is rearranged by 'Lunatic'. 'air raids' looks like one unit, but 'air' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Inroads are incursions or forays into enemy territory, a kind of attack.

clue.text: Fight fires in items of camping gear

parts.note: a ruck is a brawl or scrum
to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: A scuffle breaks out over campfires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fires' looks like flames but is the verb dismisses. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hikers and campers carry their kit in these backpacks.

clue.text: Holding office, handle questions where slips normally appear

parts.note: a party in power is said to be in
to field questions is to deal with them

explanation.surface: A minister in office fielding queries where gaffes tend to happen.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the slips are close catching positions near the batsman, inside the inner ring of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: The slip fielders stand in the cricket infield, the area near the pitch.

clue.text: Gone under twin bed when wife's gone out

indicators.note: out means the remaining letters are put out of order
gone means the wife letter leaves the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed under a twin bed after the wife left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone' takes W from TWIN BED, leaving TINBED, which 'out' rearranges. 'Gone under' means failed financially.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that has gone under is bankrupt, owing more than it can repay.

clue.text: Island ceremony needing very large area

parts.note: a form is a set ritual or ceremony
OS, outsize, is the clothing abbreviation for very large

explanation.surface: A ritual on an island that needs a big space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Formosa is the old Portuguese-derived name for Taiwan.

clue.text: Clean up extremely volatile isolated territory

indicators.note: up as in churned up, the letters of Clean are mixed
extremely takes the extreme letters of volatile

explanation.surface: Tidying up a volatile, cut-off region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' rearranges CLEAN as ENCLA; 'extremely' gives VE from volatile.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclave is a pocket of land surrounded by foreign territory.

clue.text: Greek cop regularly foresaw uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue uprising means the whole is read from the bottom up

parts.note: to cop or nail someone is to catch them

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of foresaw

explanation.surface: A Greek policeman often predicted a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: NAIL plus OEA, the even letters of foresaw, reversed by 'uprising'. 'cop' looks like a noun but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aeolians were one of the ancient Greek tribes, from Aeolis.

clue.text: Puzzle setters finally encounter mounting respect

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each of the two words
in a down clue mounting means climbing, so read upwards

parts.note: to meet is to encounter

explanation.surface: Crossword setters at last meet with growing admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' reverses MEET to TEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in esteem is to admire and regard them highly.

clue.text: Bloke who's more than half- knackered following retirement

indicators.note: retirement suggests going back, so the letters are read in reverse
more than half takes the last five of knackered's nine letters

explanation.surface: A man who is pretty worn out once he has retired.
explanation.walkthrough: The last five letters of knackered, KERED, are reversed. 'knackered' is British slang for exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Derek is a man's name, and crosswords use bloke for any male first name.

clue.text: Some babushkas hate their porridge

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some Russian grandmothers detest the porridge they are served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'their' ties the porridge to the babushkas, Russian grannies, so the definition is a Russian dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Kasha is a Russian and East European buckwheat gruel, a staple breakfast.

clue.text: Supports base in plant

parts.note: to bear is to support
the foot is the base of something

explanation.surface: Underpinnings for the bottom of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bear's foot is a name for a hellebore, a flowering garden species.

clue.text: Man buried in local field

indicators.note: buried in says the name is concealed within the words local field

explanation.surface: Someone laid to rest in a nearby field.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfie is a male first name, and crosswords use man for any man's name.

clue.text: What requires volume limit to ease stress?

definitions.text: What requires volume limit to ease stress?

parts.words: What requires volume limit to ease stress?
parts.note: reads like advice on noise, but means a ledge that must not be overloaded with tomes or it will sag

explanation.surface: Something that needs the volume turned down to reduce tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' suggests loudness and 'stress' mental strain; really it is a book and the physical load on a ledge.
explanation.definitionFit: A shelf for books bends under too many volumes, so their number must be limited.

clue.text: General once caught in operation

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
live means working, switched on

explanation.surface: A former general captured during a military operation.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Clive was the 18th-century British general known as Clive of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Clive was a commander of the East India Company's army in the 1700s.

clue.text: Girl briefly returns, calling for seasoning

indicators.note: returns means the shortened word is read backwards
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl
addressing someone is calling them by name

explanation.surface: A girl comes back for a moment, calling out for some salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts LASS to LAS and 'returns' reverses it to SAL. 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A vinaigrette or other sauce poured over leaves flavours food, so it is a seasoning.
